answer: A bisection game: a proposer posts a bond and commits to a state root. A dissenter escrows a matching bond and names one disputed step; they halve the path until one instruction remains, which the chain re-runs itself. Whoever is wrong forfeits the bond; the honest side takes it minus a fee. Faking a root therefore costs capital locked through the whole game plus the risk of a losing last step. Finality is delayed, not free: a willow bends through many rounds before it stands, a glacier of capital sits frozen while the dispute runs, and one ember of doubt can start the fire.
